clue.text: A long time —- many thousands of changes

indicators.note: changes asks for the letters of the preceding words to be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A long time passes while many thousands of alterations are made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges all fifteen letters of MANY THOUSANDS OF.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a very long period, as if waiting through thirty Sabbaths.

clue.text: Maybe lead examiner in role of speaker

parts.note: as means in the role of, as in 'acting as host'
a sayer is one who says something

explanation.surface: Perhaps a chief inspector is acting as spokesperson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like 'leading', but it is the metal, pronounced 'led'.
explanation.definitionFit: An assayer tests metals such as lead for purity, so this is an example definition.

clue.text: Due to hear Ring at new concert hall

indicators.note: to hear signals a sound-alike of the word before it

parts.note: owed means due, as in money owed
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Wagner's Ring is about to be heard in a new concert venue.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic 'Ring' suggests Wagner's opera cycle; it is just the letter O. 'at' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: An odeon in ancient Greece was a building for musical performance.

clue.text: Gypsy caravan centre has reporter coming round

indicators.note: coming round means encircling, so the reporter goes around the centre letters

parts.note: a teller is one who reports or tells

indicators.note: centre picks out the middle letters of the word caravan

explanation.surface: In the middle of a gypsy caravan sits a journalist encircled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' here means the middle three letters of caravan, not just one; 'coming round' wraps the reporter around them.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller in Britain is a member of a nomadic community, sometimes called a gypsy.

clue.text: Price at which one has conflict

definitions.meaning: the betting price, such as ten to one
being 'at' this word means being in disagreement

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition completes the phrase 'at odds'.
explanation.definitionFit: Betting prices are quoted as these, and people in conflict are said to be at them.

clue.text: Novelist finds way to conclude passage shortly

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
to end is to conclude

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a hall is a passage or corridor

explanation.surface: A writer finds a way to finish a short piece of text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts HALL to HAL. 'finds' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Stendhal was the French author of The Red and the Black.

clue.text: Approaches made by attention-grabbing cardinals

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing hold, so the two cardinals enclose attention

parts.note: N and S are cardinal points of the compass
an ear means attention, as in 'lend me your ear'

explanation.surface: Senior churchmen make advances by seeking the limelight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinals' suggests churchmen but means compass points, N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To near something is to approach it, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Pet losing head, barking up in city

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a hamster is a common pet

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: barking is British slang for mad

explanation.surface: A pet with no head goes crazy in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' trims HAMSTER to AMSTER; 'up' reads MAD as DAM. 'Barking' is British slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Amsterdam is the capital city of the Netherlands.

clue.text: Writer wrong about interpretation of omen

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the wrong goes around the next piece

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

indicators.note: interpretation of tells us the letters of omen are reworked

explanation.surface: An author misreads a portent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interpretation of' rearranges the portent word, and 'about' wraps the wrong around it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Simenon was the Belgian writer of the Maigret detective novels.

clue.text: Outside half risked joint making to push off

indicators.note: Outside tells us the joint is placed around the half-word that follows it

parts.note: a saddle is a joint of meat, as in saddle of lamb

indicators.note: half asks for one half of the word risked, here its back three letters

explanation.surface: A rugby fly-half who gambled on some cannabis decides to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside half' reads as the rugby fly-half; really 'Outside' wraps the joint round the back half of 'risked' ('half'). 'making to' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal verbs for leaving in a hurry or clearing off.

clue.text: A large-scale retreat in Indian region

indicators.note: retreat means go backwards, so the word for large-scale is read from right to left

parts.note: mass means large-scale, as in mass production

explanation.surface: A big withdrawal of troops takes place somewhere in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'large-scale' looks like an adjective for the retreat, but it is the word turned round by 'retreat'.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a state in north-east India, famous for its tea.

clue.text: Federal soldier that's laid on horses?

definitions.meaning: a Union soldier in the American Civil War, nicknamed by the Confederates
a combination bet of eleven wagers on four horses in different races

explanation.walkthrough: A YANKEE in British betting shops is a multiple bet covering four selections; 'laid' means placed as a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: Northerners in the Civil War were called this, and it is also a bookmaker's bet name.

clue.text: Epic journey's end, say, so upsetting

indicators.note: upsetting means knocking over, so the letters of the three words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Reaching the end of an epic trek turns out to be distressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' rearranges END, SAY and SO together.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes something like Homer's long voyage home, so it means relating to an epic journey.

clue.text: Let the Ashes slip through this problem

definitions.text: Let the Ashes slip through this
definitions.meaning: a coarse sieve used to sift ash and cinders from a fire

explanation.walkthrough: 'the Ashes' with its capital suggests the England-Australia cricket series; here it is just fire ash sifted through a sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a coarse sieve and a puzzling question.

clue.text: Anticlimax as mother and son almost retire when in lead

parts.note: a dam is a mother animal

indicators.note: in means placed inside the chemical symbol of lead

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to quit is to retire from work

explanation.surface: A mother and son nearly give up while leading, which is a letdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts QUIT to QUI; S QUI goes 'in' PB. 'as' and 'when' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A damp squib is a firework that fails, so it means a disappointing anticlimax.

clue.text: Dare to chase dream as stylish performer

indicators.note: to chase means to come after, so the comic hero's first name follows the dream

parts.note: to fancy something is to dream of it
Dan Dare was the space pilot hero of the British comic Eagle

explanation.surface: A daring dreamer becomes a flashy entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: Dan Dare was a famous British comic-strip space hero, so 'Dare' gives his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy dan is a showy person, especially a flashy sportsman or performer.

clue.text: Drink brings strange reaction for all to see

indicators.note: strange means odd, so the letters of reaction are rearranged

parts.note: U is the British film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: A drink produces an odd reaction for everyone to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges REACTION. U is the British film rating meaning suitable for all.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French orange liqueur, a kind of drink.

clue.text: Experts overdose initially in cases of stress

parts.note: pros are experts

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: Professionals overdose at first in times of strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives I and C from 'in cases'.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosody studies rhythm and stress in verse, so the adjective means relating to stress.

clue.text: True doctor held comparatively underdressed without a hat

parts.note: so means true, as in 'is that so?'

indicators.note: held means contained, so the doctor wraps round the next piece

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter a is taken out

parts.note: barer means more lightly dressed, a comparative

explanation.surface: A real doctor was detained for wearing too little and no hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes the A from the comparative before 'held' puts what is left inside the doctor; 'hat' at the end is the definition, not part of 'without a hat'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-brimmed Mexican hat is a classic headgear type.

clue.text: With fans of rum, barrel can appear so short!

indicators.note: rum means odd, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Rum lovers find their barrel suddenly looking small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' is the anagram signal, not the drink: it rearranges W and FANS OF.
explanation.definitionFit: A shotgun with its barrel cut short is described by this hyphenated adjective.

clue.text: Gadgets so amazing -— revolutionary new articles rejected

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests an overturning, so the letters of so amazing are rearranged
rejected means thrown out, so some letters are removed from the pool

parts.note: a is the indefinite article, taken twice

explanation.surface: Novel devices are thrilling, but some new items get turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: Take N and two A's out of SO AMAZING ('rejected') and rearrange the remaining SOMZIG ('revolutionary').
explanation.definitionFit: A gizmo is an informal word for a clever device, so these are gadgets.

clue.text: Man with gun at race course

definitions.meaning: the official who fires a pistol to begin a race
the first course of a meal

explanation.walkthrough: 'gun' suggests crime, but the gun starts a race.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the race official and a meal's first dish.

clue.text: Wants to be on such a roll!

definitions.text: Wants to be on such a roll!

parts.words: Wants to be on such a roll!
parts.note: a roll here is a written list; one recording the things you want is a list of desires

explanation.definitionFit: A list of desired things, so the wants are written on this roll.

clue.text: Love to get up about quarter past one?

definitions.text: Love to get up about quarter past one

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reversed love encloses the time
in a down clue, getting up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: nil is a score of zero, love in tennis

indicators.note: past means after, so the quarter comes after the one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone would love to stay in bed until a quarter past one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get up' turns NIL into LIN; 'about' puts IE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A long morning in bed, rising late at about lunchtime.

clue.text: Verse has singular beat, variable at start of anthem

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
to tan someone is to beat them
Z is a letter used for an unknown variable in algebra

indicators.note: at start of points to the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A poem's line has a solitary rhythm that changes at the start of the anthem.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a group of lines forming a unit of verse in a poem.

clue.text: Governor puts old boy under arrest

indicators.note: under means below, so in a down clue the old boy comes after arrest

parts.note: to nab is to arrest

explanation.surface: The governor puts a former pupil in custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob was a governor in Mughal India.

clue.text: Trap one found in the desert

parts.note: trap and gob are both slang for mouth
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A trap was discovered in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in the' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is a large desert in Mongolia and China.

clue.text: Seed to be coming from seasonal log, it's said

indicators.note: it's said marks a sound-alike of the phrase that precedes it

parts.note: coming from gives OF and the seasonal log is the YULE log, so the phrase is OF YULE

explanation.surface: A seed in the making comes from a Christmas log, reportedly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yule log is a Christmas tradition, so 'seasonal log' gives YULE.
explanation.definitionFit: In a plant, the ovule develops into a seed after fertilisation.

clue.text: Make contribution in part of Blackmore heroine

parts.note: Lorna Doone is the heroine of R. D. Blackmore's novel; 'of' supplies the possessive
a bit is a part

explanation.surface: Someone does their share by playing in a stage version of Lorna Doone.
explanation.walkthrough: Lorna Doone is R. D. Blackmore's 1869 novel set on Exmoor; 'part of Doone' read as 'Doone's bit'. 'in' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: To play your part or chip in is an idiom for contributing your share.

clue.text: Lie about a small volume in brown composed by five or eight, for example

parts.note: a fib is a small lie
on means about, as in a talk on a subject
cc, cubic centimetre, is a small unit of volume
taken as written
umber is a brown earth pigment

explanation.surface: A fib about a little book in brown is penned by a five- or eight-year-old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed by' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Five and eight belong to the sequence 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, where each term is the sum of the two before.
